guidance: A description of what a conforming server should answer, not a probe of a particular one. Servers may ignore or reject a Range header, caches and proxies may recombine parts, and a body is counted on the bytes as sent, after any content coding.
method: The header is read per RFC 9110 section 14: a range unit, an equals sign and a comma-separated list of byte ranges, where first-last gives inclusive offsets counted from zero, first- runs to the end of the representation, and -N asks for the last N bytes. An int-range with a last byte below its first byte, a missing unit, a non-numeric field or an empty range specifier makes the ranges-specifier invalid and the header is treated as ignored. A last byte at or past the representation length is replaced by the last byte of the representation, and a suffix longer than the representation selects all of it. A range is satisfiable when its first byte is below the representation length, or when it is a suffix range with a non-zero length. If at least one range is satisfiable the response is 206 with only those ranges: one part carries Content-Range bytes first-last/length, and several parts use multipart/byteranges with one Content-Range per part. If none is satisfiable the response is 416 with Content-Range bytes */length and no body. The body size is the sum of the served part lengths, and the saving is that sum against the full length, reported as a percentage with enough decimals to stay honest at the extremes. An If-Range validator that does not match discards the header before it is applied, so the whole representation is sent with 200. Sizes are whole bytes from 1 to 1,099,511,627,776 and a header may list at most 32 ranges. Everything runs in the browser with no uploads, storage or network calls.
